statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 11 percent sits in the low band, well below the block threshold, and one shared assessment covers NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON for both instruments. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC window spanning the US cash open, the S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC, the Barr speech at 14:05 UTC and the delayed post-release second leg, where the published forecast reaches the WATCH band for two hours, and again in the 19:00 UTC power hour. Oil weakness on Middle East de-escalation and a six-session semiconductor advance are treated as backdrop rather than as observed path amplifiers, and the expected Trump-Xi meeting on 24 September is scored as a Stress and Confidence factor. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ edges to the top of an unextended overnight band while Asian breadth splits
body:
The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed on 22 September at 30,732.40, up 250.04 points or 0.82 percent, inside a 30,496.43-30,770.63 range and at a fresh record close against a 22,841.42-30,770.63 annual range. Globex NQ now trades at 31,057.00, plus 28.50 points or 0.09 percent, still inside the same 30,985.25-31,070.50 overnight band that has framed the past three hourly assessments. Price has drifted from the middle of that band to 13.5 points below its high, but the band itself has not widened: it spans 85.25 points, roughly 0.27 percent. Drift toward an edge without range expansion is rotation, not the directional efficiency that denies mean reversion, and that distinction is what keeps Tail at 11 rather than in the watch band.

Cross-asset evidence is supportive but not uniformly aligned, which is the more common configuration in an orderly advance. VIX closed at 14.21, down 0.66 or 4.44 percent, far beneath the 35.30 top of its annual range. WTI trades near 89.31 dollars, down about 1.3 percent, with Brent near 98.37, down about 0.9 percent, after reports of Iranian willingness to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and the restart of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. That is geopolitical de-escalation rather than discontinuity, and it removes rather than adds a tail amplifier. Treasury yields are close to unchanged, with the latest H.15 constant maturities at 4.76 percent for the 2-year and 4.96 percent for the 10-year. Semiconductors have now closed higher six sessions running, a genuinely persistent directional tone, but the Asian tape disagrees: MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan is up 0.3 percent with Korea up 0.5 percent and Taiwan up 0.7 percent, while Chinese blue chips are down 0.5 percent and Hang Seng TECH is off about 1.5 percent. Tokyo cash is shut for the Autumnal Equinox, thinning the overnight book further.

Scheduled risk is concentrated in a narrow afternoon block. The S&P Global US flash PMIs print at 13:45 UTC, fifteen minutes after the 13:30 UTC cash open, with Governor Barr at 14:05 UTC and EIA inventories at 14:30 UTC, then a 5-year note auction at 17:00 UTC. The Trump-Xi meeting is expected on 24 September rather than today; its timing is not firmly published, so it is treated as a Stress and Confidence factor and is not carried in the event calendar. Under the fixed mapping, Tail 11 yields EA_ON and a green status for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.

lookbackSummary: The last 24 published hours cover one completed US session and its orderly overnight handover. Through the European morning of 22 September Tail sat at 12-13 with Stress in the mid-to-high 30s. Tail peaked at 21 in the 14:00 UTC cash-open hour as a trend-up regime established itself, eased to 14-17 across the mixed early afternoon, then returned to 20-21 through the 18:00-19:00 UTC power-hour block ahead of the record close. Since that close Tail has decayed monotonically from 19 to 10 and the dominant mode has reverted from trend-up to normal, which is the decay profile of an orderly advance rather than a path that denied retracement. All 24 slots carry a published assessment and none reached the blocking band.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours run from a thin, holiday-shortened Asian book through the European flash PMI block and into the densest scheduled risk of the day. Tail is held at 11-13 across the Asian and European hours, where the only checkpoints are the French, German, euro-area and UK flash PMIs between 07:15 and 08:30 UTC. It steps to 21-22 for the 13:00 and 14:00 UTC hours, which carry the US cash open, the S&P Global US flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC, the Barr speech at 14:05 UTC, EIA inventories at 14:30 UTC and the delayed second-leg window, producing the first WATCH mapping. Tail then decays to 15-17 through the US afternoon around the 17:00 UTC 5-year auction before a secondary rise to 20 in the 19:00 UTC power hour, where a record-close backdrop makes late extension plausible. Overnight values return to 12-13, with the Tokyo cash reopen at 00:00 UTC on 24 September the one identifiable structural checkpoint, and the final slot lifts marginally ahead of a denser Thursday calendar.

forecastDetail.comment: Observed drift to within 13.5 points of the overnight high while the 85-point band 30,985.25-31,070.50 stays unextended keeps the mapped state at the low-band floor, with VIX at 14.21 and nothing scheduled before 07:15 UTC.

European cash opens with regional futures about 0.4 percent higher into the French and German flash PMIs; a handover that finally breaks and holds outside the overnight band would be the first structural tell, and containment would not.

The euro-area and UK flash PMIs complete the European block; only a directional European reaction that NQ follows without a genuine pullback would lift path risk, and Tokyo remaining shut keeps cross-border flow thin.
Post-PMI European mid-morning carries no scheduled US release, so conditional risk stays minimal unless the morning is still making highs on shallow dips into the London fix window.
London midday has no catalyst and thin liquidity that normally favours range behaviour; a fresh range high carried into the US pre-market on no news would be the notable deviation.
